devotionals.passageText:
1  But there will be no gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the latter time he has made glorious the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

2 The people who walked in darkness
    have seen a great light;
those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness,
    on them has light shone.
3 You have multiplied the nation;
    you have increased its joy;
they rejoice before you
    as with joy at the harvest,
    as they are glad when they divide the spoil.
4 For the yoke of his burden,
    and the staff for his shoulder,
    the rod of his oppressor,
    you have broken as on the day of Midian.
5 For every boot of the tramping warrior in battle tumult
    and every garment rolled in blood
    will be burned as fuel for the fire.
6 For to us a child is born,
    to us a son is given;
and the government shall be upon his shoulder,
    and his name shall be called
Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God,
    Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
7 Of the increase of his government and of peace
    there will be no end,
on the throne of David and over his kingdom,
    to establish it and to uphold it
with justice and with righteousness
    from this time forth and forevermore.
The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
devotionals.praypoints:
Matthew 24:13-14 "But the one who endures to the end will be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come." 
  Pray for the gospel witness of the church, especially in places where persecution is strongly experienced.
  Pray for God to grant endurance and strength to these believers to shine His light even in the darkest places.

questions.text: Context // Read Isaiah 8:20-22. How is it related to the descriptions found in 9:1-2? (Note: the places described in v1a and 1b all refer to the same regions, which were the first places in the northern kingdom of Israel to fall to Assyrian empire around 733 BC.)

Observation // From vv1-3, contrast the previous and future conditions of the places described. From vv4-6, what are the three reasons given for this change in circumstances? Which of these is the main reason? (Hint: read "for" to mean "because")

Meaning // This week's Advent theme is Hope. How does today's passage point us to Hope? How would the arrival of the prophesied child and his reign secure this hope? (Think about the descriptions in vv6b-7.)

Application // Jesus is the ultimate fulfilment of Isaiah's prophecy. Read John 1:1-5, 9-13. Have you come to believe in Jesus as the true Hope and Light of the world who gives life and enables you to become a child of God? Take time to give thanks to God for giving us the hope that is found in Jesus alone.

devotionals.title: Hope In A God Who Acts (by Pr Evangeline Chong)
devotionals.passageText:
1 Oh that you would rend the heavens and come down,
    that the mountains might quake at your presence——
2 as when fire kindles brushwood
    and the fire causes water to boil——
to make your name known to your adversaries,
    and that the nations might tremble at your presence!
3 When you did awesome things that we did not look for,
    you came down, the mountains quaked at your presence.
4 From of old no one has heard
    or perceived by the ear,
no eye has seen a God besides you,
    who acts for those who wait for him.
5 You meet him who joyfully works righteousness,
    those who remember you in your ways.
Behold, you were angry, and we sinned;
    in our sins we have been a long time, and shall we be saved?
6 We have all become like one who is unclean,
    and all our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment.
We all fade like a leaf,
    and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
7 There is no one who calls upon your name,
    who rouses himself to take hold of you;
for you have hidden your face from us,
    and have made us melt in the hand of our iniquities.

8 But now, O Lord, you are our Father;
    we are the clay, and you are our potter;
    we are all the work of your hand.
9 Be not so terribly angry, O Lord,
    and remember not iniquity forever.
    Behold, please look, we are all your people.
devotionals.article:
When you did awesome things that we did not look for,
you came down, the mountains quaked at your presence.
From of old no one has heard or perceived by the ear, no eye has seen a God besides you, who acts for those who wait for him.
Isaiah 64:3-4

In Israel's history, God's coming down to Mount Sinai (Exodus 19) marked the presence of God in their midst. With thunder, lightning and a dense cloud, the holy God descended to speak to His people and prepare them for a new life in His presence after their freedom from slavery in Egypt. 
In this prayer (following the prophecies of the punishment of exile to Assyria in Chap 1-39 and Babylon in Chap 40-55), Isaiah cries out in distress to God who judges sin yet draws near to act for the good of Israel.
Earlier, Isaiah had prophesied God's promised action: "the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel" (Isaiah 7:14). And we now know that God was preparing to act for those in distress! Doing the most unthinkable thing, He sent Jesus to the cross to give humanity a way out of our sins and reconcile us to Himself.  

As we begin the season of Advent, a time of reflection on Jesus' promised arrival, both in memory of His incarnation and in anticipation of His return in glory, let us keep our eyes open to see what God is doing, acting in power and love for the good of our world and in our lives.
Let us hold on to the hope of a God "who acts for those who wait for Him" (v4) and who will come down again to dwell among His people again.
devotionals.prayer: When all around us is devastation and hopelessness, Lord, renew our eyes to see You at work in our different situations today, so that we may continue to hold on to You, our Living Hope. Amen.
devotionals.praypoints:
Take time to pray for your own personal needs.
Walk with God through every aspect of your life —— your personal, family, work, school, community, and church aspects of your life. Say, "Speak whatever to me, Lord, I'm listening!"

questions.text: Looking back to look forward: Think of a time God acted in a way you did not expect or look for. How does remembering that moment shape the way you approach this season of Advent?

devotionals.title: Hope In A God Who Is Faithful (by Pr Evangeline Chong)
devotionals.passageText:
3 Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

4 I give thanks to my God always for you because of the grace of God that was given you in Christ Jesus, 5 that in every way you were enriched in him in all speech and all knowledge—— 6 even as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you—— 7 so that you are not lacking in any gift, as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ, 8 who will sustain you to the end, guiltless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. 9 God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
devotionals.article:
In 2000, a Barna survey showed that 75% agreed that the Bible teaches that "God only helps those who help themselves." This idea has roots in ancient Greek thought and Algernon Sidney gave it its form in 1698, yet it could not be further from the truth. The Asian culture of distant fathers and virtues of self-reliance and perseverance feed even more into this notion. No wonder many children of God who acknowledge Jesus only as Savior, struggle and fight as much as the rest of the world to fend and provide for themselves, living like spiritual orphans as if the God who calls Himself their Father is not interested in their daily lives. As such, many see a relationship with God as just merely a church routine of ever-growing expectations of prayer, faith and activity without knowing the faithful God. 
Yet 1 Corinthians begins with reminding God's people of the glorious hope they have in Christ where the church has been given all things it needs: Grace of God (v4), riches in God (all speech and knowledge v5), all gifts (v7). On top of all these, as we await Jesus' second Advent, we have a great Savior who will sustain us guiltless to the end (v8). 
Our God, the "Father to the fatherless" (Psalm 68:5) is faithful, not a neglectful parent who only drops in to check our homework. He is a God who helped the "utterly helpless, (for) Christ came at just the right time and died for us sinners (Romans 5:6 NLT)." He sent Jesus when no one was looking (Isaiah 64:3) so we can trust Him for the everyday and trust Jesus to return. This gives us a restedness in life and hope as we await the second advent of Jesus.
devotionals.prayer:
Father, thank you that in Christ I lack nothing and that you are faithful to the end.
Forgive me for living as though I must earn my place or provide for myself.
Teach me to rest in your grace and to wait with hope for the day Jesus returns. Amen.
devotionals.praypoints:
- Pray that every member of the family would personally know and trust the Lord, growing in repentance, faith, and obedience to Christ.
- Ask God to shape the home into a place where Scripture is honored, prayer is practiced, and Christlike love is demonstrated daily.
- Pray that the family would resist worldly influences and instead pursue holiness, faithfulness, and joyful service to God.

devotionals.passageText:
26 In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, 27 to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David. And the virgin's name was Mary. 28 And he came to her and said, "Greetings, O favored one, the Lord is with you!" 29 But she was greatly troubled at the saying, and tried to discern what sort of greeting this might be. 30 And the angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. 31 And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. 32 He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David, 33 and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end."

34 And Mary said to the angel, "How will this be, since I am a virgin?"

35 And the angel answered her, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be called holy——the Son of God. 36 And behold, your relative Elizabeth in her old age has also conceived a son, and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren. 37 For nothing will be impossible with God." 38 And Mary said, "Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word." And the angel departed from her.
devotionals.praypoints:
- For a smooth and fruitful mobile clinic ministry in the prison and villages.
- For open doors to conduct the clinics and minister to the inmates, while our partner NGO has opportunities to share the Gospel with them.
- For God's wisdom upon the team, good relationships with the authorities, and favour in every step, so that both the medical and Gospel ministries can be carried out effectively for His glory.
- Pray for safety for the team as they travel on the road

questions.text: Context // What do you recall from Tuesday's passage in Isaiah 9:1-7? How is today's passage connected (see Isa 9:6-7)?
Observation // What did the angel Gabriel instruct Mary about the child she was going to conceive? How did he describe the child? What did Mary ask Gabriel and what was his response?

Meaning // Compare the description of Jesus by Gabriel to the child prophesied in Isaiah 9:1-7. How does this serve to identify Jesus as the prophesied child? What else do we learn about Jesus' character and reign through Isaiah 9:17?

Application // Jesus' birth marked the beginning of the ultimate fulfilment of Isaiah's prophecy, while His glorious return as King will complete it. How can the certainty of Jesus' return give you a steadfast hope amidst the challenges you experience in life and all that is wrong in the world?

devotionals.praypoints:
- Pray for countries and regions experiencing strife
- For God to protect the innocent and help to reach them
- For peace to be established, and justice to prevail

questions.text: What were some high points in this week? When did I experience joy and life?
What were some low points in this week? When did I feel sad, resentment, anger, frustration?
How did I see God work in my life this week? How did God answer prayer?
What is one thing that God said to me about the happenings of my week?
What is one thing that you can ask God in response to what He is saying to you? Commit this to God in prayer.

devotionals.article:
An Advent Prayer (prayerist.com)
Dear God,
In this Advent of expectation draw us together in unity,
that our praise and worship might echo in these walls and also through our lives.
In this Advent of expectation draw us together in mission,
that the hope within might be the song we sing, and the melody of our lives.
In this Advent of expectation draw us together in service,
that the path we follow might lead us from a stable to a glimpse of eternity.
Amen.
devotionals.praypoints:
"As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another." ——Proverbs 27:17
- Pray that church members will help each other grow in faith and challenge one another to live for Jesus, just as iron sharpens iron.
- Pray that through fellowship and teaching, everyone will grow stronger in their discipleship, supporting one another in love and obedience.
- Pray that the church family will stand together in guidance, prayer, and encouragement, helping each other through challenges and keeping each other focused on Christ.

devotionals.article:
Unlike most people I know, who prefer to sleep in complete darkness and would even go as far as using an eye mask to block out every bit of light, I've always felt more comfortable with a small light left on. Even a faint night light in the corner brings a quiet sense of peace and safety.

I wonder if you've ever felt that way, not just at night, but in life itself?  There are seasons when a shadow or darkness hangs over everything: worry about job security and the rising cost of living, pressure to keep up with work, studies, and family expectations, strained relationships, or burdens we carry in silence.  It can feel like being in a long, dark tunnel, with no light in sight, wondering when we'll finally come out the other side.

That is exactly where God's people stood when the prophet spoke these words in Isaiah 9:1—7. They lived in deep darkness —— oppressed, afraid, and longing for hope. In the middle of the darkness, God gave a promise that brought hope:

"The people walking in darkness have seen a great light;
on those living in the land of deep darkness
a light has dawned." (Isaiah 9:2)

This wasn't a promise about a lamp beside a bed. It was the promise of Jesus —— the Great Light who was coming to shine in our deepest shadows.  Isaiah tells us exactly who this Child is:

The Wonderful Counsellor who understands us completely.
The Mighty God who possesses the power to save and deliver us.
The Everlasting Father who loves and cares for us always.
The Prince of Peace who brings wholeness that the world cannot give. 

He came not only to show us the way, but to be the Way. He came to break the power of sin and fear, bring hope into our darkness, and establish a kingdom of peace that will never end.

Whatever darkness you may be facing today, remember this: the Light has already come. No darkness is too deep for Jesus. Whether you are struggling with fear, sadness, confusion, or sin, His light is greater than all of it. You do not need to fix your life before coming to Him. Come as you are and let His light shine into your situation.

But Jesus did not come only to shine His light on us. He calls us to walk in that light. Just as the people in Isaiah's day were invited to follow God's ways, we too are called to turn away from sin and follow Jesus each day through prayer, reading His Word, and obeying Him.

We will still face challenges, but we do not walk alone. Jesus goes before us, guides us, and strengthens us. As we keep our eyes on Him, His light will lead us through the darkness and fill our hearts with hope, peace, and joy.
devotionals.praypoints:
1 Peter 4:10 "As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace."
- Pray that you would faithfully use your spiritual gifts to serve others for God's glory.
- Ask God to give a generous and hospitable heart toward those who need encouragement or support.
- Pray that your service would strengthen others and point them toward Christ.

questions.text: What "darkness" am I walking through right now? Is it fear, uncertainty, guilt, loneliness, or something else? Name it honestly before the Lord.
In what ways have I been trying to find light or comfort apart from Jesus? Through distraction, control, success, or people? What would it look like to turn toward Him instead?
Which name of Jesus in Isaiah 9:6 do I need most today—— His wisdom (Wonderful Counsellor), His strength (Mighty God), His care (Everlasting Father), or His calm (Prince of Peace)? Why?
Who in my life is still walking in darkness and needs to hear about this Great Light? How can I reflect His light to them this week?
